name: Cinnamon Satin
lede: Cinnamon Satin is a dusty, deep pink from the Crayola crayon list, sharing only its name with the two older, browner Cinnamon colors from Ridgway's 1912 standard.

sections.title: A modern name, not a Ridgway one
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[france-rose]], [[blush]], [[cinnamon-satin]] and [[carmine-red]], at 2.8, 3.1, 3.8 and 4.8 ΔE [2]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would place this swatch in the category deep pink, 8.0 units from that block's centroid [2]. 

The name keeps the spice word *cinnamon* for its warmth, not its brown, pairing it with *satin* for sheen rather than hue; the actual color sits among the pinks, not the browns of [[cinnamon-drab]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Cinnamon Satin covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only one work, a 1924 still life by Patrick Henry Bruce, as photographed [3]. That makes it one of the rarest colors we track in the archive, essentially absent from paintings before the twentieth century [3]. The scarcity fits a crayon color with no claimed history before its listing [3].

origin.named_after: the spice cinnamon, for warmth, and satin, for sheen; origin otherwise undocumented
